messages.subject: SPDE range issues
parts:
Hey everyone, 

I've run into some issues trying to develop a hurdle model for a time series data from a freshwater lake. Right now I am just trying to get the binomial part working properly.

The biomass for the species I'm trying to model has been reduced to nearly 0 in recent years, and the the species is caught in <10% of trawls in recent year compared to >60% in the early 2000's






I have been having a lot of issues with the range of the spde, where the range always seems to come out above 600km (which is about the range of the lake from north to south). More than 90% of catch occurs in the north basin of the lake (large basin in the mesh plot below) so I suspect that might be one of the main issues.

I've looked at many posts in this discussion group as well as the hurdle model outlined here (https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/spde-gitbook/ch-stapp.html#sec:hgst). 

I've tried altering the priors in the inla.spde2.pcmatern() function, adding the correct = TRUE  to the control.inla() argument, adding in local random effects via "iid" models for both station and each observation to try and deal with local overdispersion, and countless other tweaks.

At this point I'm not sure what else I can do, otherwise than conclude that maybe the spde model may nor work for this system. 

I've included the code used to run the binomial model below. Any suggestions/guidance  would be appreciated! I can also provide some files and code to run the model and set up the workspace.

Thanks in advance,
Colin


####
#
## Set up the INLA model
#
####

# Step 1. Create the mesh
max.edge <- 4
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(max.edge = c(3, 10) * max.edge,
                     boundary = StudyArea, cutoff = 4) 
plot(mesh)
mesh$n # aim for 800 to 900 nodes for testing - Zuur course guideline
points(modData$Station_X, modData$Station_Y, pch = 19, col = 2)


# Step 2: Create temporal mesh 
# Data goes from 2002 to 2019, but define knots at 2005, 2010 & 2015
Knots <- c(2005, 2010, 2015)
mesh.t <- inla.mesh.1d(loc = Knots)
mesh.t$loc
mesh.t$n  #We have 3 random fields


# Step 3. Define the weighting factors a_ik (also called the projector matrix).
A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, 
                      loc = cbind(modData$Station_X, modData$Station_Y),
                      group.mesh = mesh.t,
                      group = modData$Year,
                      n.group = mesh.t$n) 


# Step 4 Define the SPDE.
spde <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh,
                            alpha = 1.5, ### give it some flexibility # https://groups.google.com/g/r-inla-discussion-group/c/ZhZVu8YPI8I/m/pUUWL1UZBAAJ
                            prior.range = c(100, 0.9), ### P(practic.range < 100) = 0.9 
                            prior.sigma = c(5, 0.1),   ### P(sigma > 5) = 0.1
                            constr = FALSE)


# Step 4. Define the spatial field for the binomial model
field.z.idx <- inla.spde.make.index(
  name = 'x',
  n.spde = spde$n.spde,
  n.group = mesh.t$n)


5: Create the stack for binomial model
stk.z <- inla.stack(
  tag = 'Fit.bern',
  data = list(Y = cbind(modData$CATCH), link = 1),
  A = list(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, A), 
  effects = list(z.intercept = rep(1, nrow(modData)),
                 z.year = modData$Year,
                 z.station = modData$Station_Code,
                 z.water_depth = modData$water_depth, 
                 z.temperature = modData$temperature,
                 z.secchi = modData$secchi,
                 z.trawl_depth = modData$trawl_depth,
                 index.z = 1:nrow(modData), # add local dispersion effect - https://groups.google.com/g/r-inla-discussion-group/c/ZhZVu8YPI8I
                 field.z.idx))

# simple model running only intercept, random effect for each obs, rw1 for year trend and spde model.
form.z <- Y ~ -1 +
  z.intercept + 
  # z.temperature +
  # z.water_depth +
  # z.trawl_depth + 
  # z.secchi + 
  f(index.z, model = "iid") +
  # f(z.station, model = "iid") +
  f(z.year, model = "rw1") + 
  f(x, model = spde, group = x.group,
    control.group = list(model = "ar1")) 


mod.z <- inla(form.z,
             family = c("binomial"),
             control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stk.z), 
                                      compute = TRUE, link = link),
             data = inla.stack.data(stk.z),
             control.inla = list(strategy = 'adaptive',
                                 correct = TRUE), # have tried adding this thru suggestion in INLA discussion group
                                 # correct.factor = 5), # have tried adding this thru suggestion in INLA discussion group
             control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE,
                                    cpo = TRUE, config = TRUE))


summary(mod.z)

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] SPDE range issues
parts:
It sounds like the covariates don’t capture the strong north/south-gradient, forcing the latent field to capture it instead, which requires a long range. Have you considered adding northing&easting as covariates, to help capture the large scale behaviour?

Finn

I just tried to add in a northing covariate and the range decreased slightly, but was still 444.

I have tried using a basin as a covariate, which is a 3 level factor (south basin, narrows, north basin). That helps to sort the data into discrete bins in the northward direction, however that still doesn't reduce the range (~610).

Colin

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] SPDE range issues
parts:
The transition between such large scale indicator variables is sharp, which may force the latent field to compensate for the transitions.
But one important question is this: why do you consider a long range to be a problem? The answer would depend on what you’re trying to accomplish with the model.
If the covariates don’t capture all the large scale structure, but there is also uncaptured short range details, you may need two latent fields; one to capture large scale, and one to capture small scale.

Finn

On 30 Sep 2020, at 18:50, Colin <colinros...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿Hey Finn thanks for the advice.

I just tried to add in a northing covariate and the range decreased slightly, but was still 444.

I have tried using a basin as a covariate, which is a 3 level factor (south basin, narrows, north basin). That helps to sort the data into discrete bins in the northward direction, however that still doesn't reduce the range (~610).

Colin

On Wednesday, September 30, 2020 at 12:34:40 PM UTC-5 finn.l...@gmail.com wrote:
It sounds like the covariates don’t capture the strong north/south-gradient, forcing the latent field to capture it instead, which requires a long range. Have you considered adding northing&easting as covariates, to help capture the large scale behaviour?

Finn

On 30 Sep 2020, at 18:20, Colin <colinros...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿Hey everyone, 


I've run into some issues trying to develop a hurdle model for a time series data from a freshwater lake. Right now I am just trying to get the binomial part working properly.

The biomass for the species I'm trying to model has been reduced to nearly 0 in recent years, and the the species is caught in <10% of trawls in recent year compared to >60% in the early 2000's






I have been having a lot of issues with the range of the spde, where the range always seems to come out above 600km (which is about the range of the lake from north to south). More than 90% of catch occurs in the north basin of the lake (large basin in the mesh plot below) so I suspect that might be one of the main issues.

I've looked at many posts in this discussion group as well as the hurdle model outlined here (https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/spde-gitbook/ch-stapp.html#sec:hgst). 

I've tried altering the priors in the inla.spde2.pcmatern() function, adding the correct = TRUE  to the control.inla() argument, adding in local random effects via "iid" models for both station and each observation to try and deal with local overdispersion, and countless other tweaks.

At this point I'm not sure what else I can do, otherwise than conclude that maybe the spde model may nor work for this system. 

I've included the code used to run the binomial model below. Any suggestions/guidance  would be appreciated! I can also provide some files and code to run the model and set up the workspace.

Thanks in advance,
Colin


####
#
## Set up the INLA model
#
####

# Step 1. Create the mesh
max.edge <- 4
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(max.edge = c(3, 10) * max.edge,
                     boundary = StudyArea, cutoff = 4) 
plot(mesh)
mesh$n # aim for 800 to 900 nodes for testing - Zuur course guideline
points(modData$Station_X, modData$Station_Y, pch = 19, col = 2)


# Step 2: Create temporal mesh 
# Data goes from 2002 to 2019, but define knots at 2005, 2010 & 2015
Knots <- c(2005, 2010, 2015)
mesh.t <- inla.mesh.1d(loc = Knots)
mesh.t$loc
mesh.t$n  #We have 3 random fields


# Step 3. Define the weighting factors a_ik (also called the projector matrix).
A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, 
                      loc = cbind(modData$Station_X, modData$Station_Y),
                      group.mesh = mesh.t,
                      group = modData$Year,
                      n.group = mesh.t$n) 


# Step 4 Define the SPDE.
spde <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh,
                            alpha = 1.5, ### give it some flexibility # https://groups.google.com/g/r-inla-discussion-group/c/ZhZVu8YPI8I/m/pUUWL1UZBAAJ
                            prior.range = c(100, 0.9), ### P(practic.range < 100) = 0.9 
                            prior.sigma = c(5, 0.1),   ### P(sigma > 5) = 0.1
                            constr = FALSE)


# Step 4. Define the spatial field for the binomial model
field.z.idx <- inla.spde.make.index(
  name = 'x',
  n.spde = spde$n.spde,
  n.group = mesh.t$n)


5: Create the stack for binomial model
stk.z <- inla.stack(
  tag = 'Fit.bern',
  data = list(Y = cbind(modData$CATCH), link = 1),
  A = list(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, A), 
  effects = list(z.intercept = rep(1, nrow(modData)),
                 z.year = modData$Year,
                 z.station = modData$Station_Code,
                 z.water_depth = modData$water_depth, 
                 z.temperature = modData$temperature,
                 z.secchi = modData$secchi,
                 z.trawl_depth = modData$trawl_depth,
                 index.z = 1:nrow(modData), # add local dispersion effect - https://groups.google.com/g/r-inla-discussion-group/c/ZhZVu8YPI8I
                 field.z.idx))

# simple model running only intercept, random effect for each obs, rw1 for year trend and spde model.
form.z <- Y ~ -1 +
  z.intercept + 
  # z.temperature +
  # z.water_depth +
  # z.trawl_depth + 
  # z.secchi + 
  f(index.z, model = "iid") +
  # f(z.station, model = "iid") +
  f(z.year, model = "rw1") + 
  f(x, model = spde, group = x.group,
    control.group = list(model = "ar1")) 


mod.z <- inla(form.z,
             family = c("binomial"),
             control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stk.z), 
                                      compute = TRUE, link = link),
             data = inla.stack.data(stk.z),
             control.inla = list(strategy = 'adaptive',
                                 correct = TRUE), # have tried adding this thru suggestion in INLA discussion group
                                 # correct.factor = 5), # have tried adding this thru suggestion in INLA discussion group
             control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE,
                                    cpo = TRUE, config = TRUE))


summary(mod.z)

parts: Sorry if I am misunderstanding, but is it possible that your prior for the range is misspecified?  You have:

# Step 4 Define the SPDE.
spde <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh,
                            alpha = 1.5, ### give it some flexibility # https://groups.google.com/g/r-inla-discussion-group/c/ZhZVu8YPI8I/m/pUUWL1UZBAAJ

                            constr = FALSE)
I would have expected that if you want the range to be small you'd have ''prior.range = c(100, 0.05)". With ''prior.range = c(100, 0.9)", are you forcing it to be large?
